To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have obtained the most convincing evidence to date for the existence of a T Tauriiike accretion phase in very low mass stars and brown dwarfs.
we find strong evidence for ongoing accretion from circumstellar disks in a sample of young very low mass objects.
(1) young brown dwarfs show strong Hα emission, (2) some of them show broad Hα profiles indicative of accretion, and (3) the lowest mass accretor to date is an object of spectral type M8.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation, evolution, and structure of stars and planets, and with their interaction with the environment.
the origin and early evolutionary history of brown dwarfs and planetary mass objects.
the study of the physical properties and evolutionary status of very low mass objects, and the implications of these results for the origin and evolution of substellar and planetary mass objects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the brown dwarfs are not accreting at the present time but they have accreted in the past and that they are not in a T Tauris stage but they were in a T Taurus stage.
the T Tauri accretion phase is a common phenomenon for all low-mass objects.
the Hα profiles of young brown dwarfs are similar to those of T Tauri-type stars.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
young substellar objects are born with disks and accretion, and that the disk and accretion phases last for longer times in substellar objects than in stars.
young substellar objects are not simply scaled-down versions of stars, but that their properties are more complex and varied.
the T Tauri accretion phase may not be limited to stars, and may extend to objects with mass as low as 0.01 M ☉.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Hα line can be used to identify very low mass accreting sources, which is crucial for studying the early evolution of brown dwarfs and planets.
the accretion process in very low mass stars and brown dwarfs appears to be similar to that in higher mass classical T Tauris.
the T Tauri phase is not limited to stars.
